about_blocks.text: About Village of Hope Eston in Eston, Saskatchewan
about_blocks.html: About Village of Hope Eston in Eston, Saskatchewan

about_blocks.text: Village of Hope Eston is a Christian residential program for adults trying to get free of drug and alcohol addiction. It runs on the former Eston College campus in Eston, a farming town in west-central Saskatchewan, and the centre describes it as a ten-month regeneration program. Students live on campus, attend classes in the morning and work in the afternoon. Its program pages, its recovery.com profile and 2025 local news coverage all describe a program for men.
about_blocks.html: Village of Hope Eston is a Christian residential program for adults trying to get free of drug and alcohol addiction. It runs on the former Eston College campus in Eston, a farming town in west-central Saskatchewan, and the centre describes it as a ten-month regeneration program. Students live on campus, attend classes in the morning and work in the afternoon. Its program pages, its recovery.com profile and 2025 local news coverage all describe a program for men.

about_blocks.text: The program moves through five phases. A roughly four-week introduction covers the basics and Christian living. Orientation looks at how addiction has damaged relationships with God, family and others, and includes the Sociogram, where the men tell each other how they see one another. Regeneration teaches the physical and psychological effects of addiction through Biblical counselling, classes and small groups. Inner Healing deals with root issues such as childhood abuse or rejection, and Discipleship turns the focus toward serving others.

about_blocks.text: Work is a big part of each day. Students bake for the Village of Hope bakery, which sells cinnamon buns, bread and cheese sticks to the public, and they go out on landscaping and off-site work crews. The centre says the aim is a good work ethic and skills people can use in a job afterwards.

about_blocks.text: The rules are strict. Tobacco, TV, radio and the internet are not allowed, phone calls are for emergencies, and there are no weekends off during the 10 months. Families can visit on Sunday afternoons after the first three weeks, or join the 11am church service and stay for a meal.

about_blocks.text: There is a $1,200 entrance fee, income-based and non-refundable, and staff help students apply for EI sickness benefits or social assistance to cover monthly costs. Donations, the Hope Partners giving program and the bakery and work crews pay for the rest. Co-founders Bishop Märt Vähi and Rev. Andrew Vähi lead the ministry, with Alex Parsons as program director. Graduates can stay another year in Servant Leader Training.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Village of Hope Eston

faqs.question: What kind of program is Village of Hope Eston?

answer_blocks.text: Village of Hope Eston is a Christian residential recovery program for adults with drug and alcohol problems, run on a campus in Eston, Saskatchewan. Students live on site for about 10 months and work through classes on orientation, regeneration, inner healing and discipleship, alongside daily work. The centre calls itself a regeneration program and uses Biblical counselling, classroom teaching and small groups.
answer_blocks.html: Village of Hope Eston is a Christian residential recovery program for adults with drug and alcohol problems, run on a campus in Eston, Saskatchewan. Students live on site for about 10 months and work through classes on orientation, regeneration, inner healing and discipleship, alongside daily work. The centre calls itself a regeneration program and uses Biblical counselling, classroom teaching and small groups.

faqs.question: Is the program for men or women?

answer_blocks.text: The program pages, the recovery.com profile and 2025 local news coverage all describe a program for men. The home page of the centre's website mentions men and women, so call 306-962-3000 to confirm whether women are accepted at the Eston campus.

faqs.question: How much does Village of Hope Eston cost?

answer_blocks.text: There is a $1,200 entrance fee, which the centre says is income-based and non-refundable. Staff help each student apply for government support such as EI sickness benefits or social assistance to cover monthly costs. The rest of the program is paid for by donations, fundraising and the centre's own social enterprises.

faqs.question: Does Village of Hope Eston offer detox?

answer_blocks.text: No. The centre's website does not describe a detox or medical withdrawal service, and recovery.com lists detox as not offered. Medications are handed over at intake and given out under staff direction, so talk to your doctor and the intake team about withdrawal care before you arrive.

faqs.question: Where is Village of Hope Eston?

answer_blocks.text: The campus is at 730 1st Street East in Eston, a small town in west-central Saskatchewan. It is about 2 hours 45 minutes from Saskatoon and about 3.5 hours from Regina, and Kindersley is around 45 minutes away. The mailing address is P.O. Box 490, Eston, SK S0L 1A0.

faqs.question: What does a typical day look like?

answer_blocks.text: Students are up at 6am, eat breakfast at 6:30 and spend 7am on chores, devotions and journaling. Classes run from 8 to 10:30am, followed by work until supper at 5:30pm. Evenings have sports, study, prayer meetings, worship and movie nights, with the odd outing off campus.

faqs.question: What are the rules during the program?

answer_blocks.text: Tobacco is not allowed, and having drugs or alcohol means immediate dismissal. Students do not use TV, radio or the internet, phone calls are limited to emergencies, and there are no trips to town or weekends off during the 10 months. Letter writing is encouraged as a way to rebuild family ties.
